stories.headline: Eight-week road closure near Chatteris
stories.brief: Drivers in the Fens are being warned of an upcoming road closure near Chatteris. A stretch of road in Cambridgeshire is set to be shut for eight weeks to allow for essential repair work to take place. Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly while these works are carried out.

stories.headline: Nominations open for 2027 Fenland Citizen Business Awards
stories.brief:
Nominations are now being accepted for the 2027 Fenland Citizen Business Awards. Accountancy firm Whitings LLP, which has offices in March, Wisbech, and Ely, has returned as the headline sponsor for the event. The awards recognise local success across eight categories, including Business of the Year, Best New Start-Up, and Employer of the Year.

Businesses, individuals, and charities are encouraged to enter before the deadline at 5pm on Wednesday, January 6. The winners will be announced during a black-tie ceremony held at the Wisbech St Mary Sports and Community Centre on Friday, March 19, 2027. Further details regarding entry criteria and categories are available on the Fenland Business Awards website.

stories.headline: Norfolk County Council confirms David Walliams books to remain in libraries
stories.brief:
Norfolk County Council has announced that books by author David Walliams will stay on library shelves across the county. Despite recent allegations of misconduct against the comedian, the council confirmed that titles including Gangsta Granny and Mr Stink remain available for loan.

Councillor Pat Gould stated that the authority follows established ethical principles regarding its collections. The council maintains that books are kept unless there is a legal reason for their removal. Officials added that all library stock is subject to regular reviews to ensure collections meet the needs of local residents.

stories.headline: Long-serving DJ retires after half a century
stories.brief: A veteran DJ has concluded a 50-year career at the same venue where they first started. The performer marked the end of their five-decade tenure by returning to the club where they originally began their professional journey.

stories.headline: Proposed Chittering data centre could provide heat for local glasshouses
stories.brief: Plans have been submitted for a new data centre near Chittering. The proposal includes a system designed to capture waste heat generated by the facility. This heat could then be repurposed to warm nearby commercial glasshouses. No further details regarding the development timeline or the scale of the project have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Two arrests following fire at derelict Cambridgeshire hotel
stories.brief: Two people have been arrested following a large fire at a derelict hotel in Cambridgeshire. Emergency services were called to the scene to tackle the blaze at the abandoned property. Police have confirmed that two individuals are currently in custody in connection with the incident. No further details regarding the cause of the fire or the location of the building have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Men’s mental health group plans expansion into March
stories.brief:
The award-winning peer support group ‘Alright Mate?’ is planning to expand its services into March following the success of its Wisbech branch. The organisation, which provides a space for men to talk openly and reduce isolation, is currently in early discussions with the Fenland Primary Care Network regarding the move. While specific details such as venues and launch dates are yet to be confirmed, organisers hope to begin operations in 2027.

The group is now seeking support for this next phase of development. They are looking for community venues in March, male volunteers to act as facilitators, and local partners. Anyone interested in supporting the initiative is encouraged to contact the secretary at secretaryalrightmatefenland@gmail.com.

stories.headline: Norfolk zoo founder and conservationist Ken Sims dies aged 85
stories.brief:
Tributes have been paid to Ken Sims, the founder of Thrigby Hall Wildlife Gardens, who has died at the age of 85. Born and raised in King’s Lynn, Mr Sims passed away on October 25. He established the popular Norfolk attraction in 1979 and was widely recognised for his global contributions to animal conservation. 

Throughout his career, Mr Sims served as a zoo inspector and held senior roles with the Zoological Society of London. Colleagues have praised his vision and determination, noting his significant work in protecting threatened species. His family, who remain local to the King’s Lynn area, described him as a highly respected figure in the international animal community.

stories.headline: NHS dental access for children in North East Cambridgeshire under review
stories.brief: Access to NHS dental services for children in North East Cambridgeshire is currently being examined. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the availability of dental care for young people in the region has been placed under the spotlight. No further details regarding the scope of this review or potential changes to local services have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over potential service cuts in West Norfolk
stories.brief:
Liberal Democrat councillor Rob Colwell is calling for greater transparency regarding proposed service cuts across West Norfolk. While the Queen Elizabeth Hospital’s 24-hour A&E remains protected, maternity and children’s inpatient services are still under review. 

Meanwhile, Norfolk County Council is considering budget reductions that could impact road maintenance, including a five per cent cut to the priority gritting network. Other proposals include increased costs for post-16 transport and reduced household waste disposal services. Councillor Colwell is urging residents to participate in ongoing public consultations before the December deadlines. The main budget consultation closes on December 7, with the post-16 transport consultation ending on December 15. Residents are encouraged to share how these potential changes would affect their daily lives.

stories.headline: New youth employment hub to open in Wisbech
stories.brief: A new employment hub for young people is set to open in Wisbech. The project follows the successful implementation of a similar scheme in Peterborough. Further details regarding the opening date or the specific location of the new facility have not yet been released.

stories.headline: NHS child health sessions to be held at fire station
stories.brief: Families in the area will soon have access to new child health services. NHS sessions for children are set to be hosted at a local fire station. The initiative aims to provide health support within the community setting. Further details regarding the schedule and specific services available are expected to be released soon.

stories.headline: Police investigate potential links between ram raids
stories.brief: Police are investigating whether a series of ram raids could be connected. Officers are currently looking into the incidents, which have been described as devastating. No further details regarding the specific locations or dates of the crimes have been released at this time. Authorities are continuing their enquiries into the matter.

stories.headline: New documentary to capture the history of West Norfolk
stories.brief:
A new 60-minute documentary, currently in development, aims to preserve the history and achievements of West Norfolk for future generations. Titled ‘Under the West Norfolk Skies’, the film is a partnership between West Norfolk Council and the Lynn-based production company RFA Media.

The project will explore ten key themes, including local industry, royal connections, and the area’s relationship with the River Great Ouse. It will examine the borough’s development since 1974 while tracing its deeper historical roots. The production team is currently gathering archive material and conducting interviews, with plans to make sections of the film available across digital platforms to ensure the borough's story remains accessible to a wide audience.

stories.headline: Plans submitted to convert former Wisbech funeral home into nine dwellings
stories.brief:
A planning application has been submitted to Fenland District Council to transform a vacant former funeral home on Alexandra Road in Wisbech. The proposal, put forward by Andrew Bennett on behalf of Fitzroy Highgate Ltd, seeks to create six houses and three flats at the site. 

The project involves demolishing part of the existing structure facing Love Lane to make way for a new two-storey building. The plans also include a small second-floor extension on the Alexandra Road side. If approved, the development will retain an outdoor courtyard for resident use, with potential space for cycle storage. The site has remained empty for more than three years.

stories.headline: Caring Together Charity opens first shop in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A new charity shop has opened its doors in King’s Lynn town centre today. Located on the High Street at the site of the former Cancer Research store, the shop is the first fundraising outlet for Caring Together. The charity provides advice and support to unpaid carers across Norfolk, Cambridgeshire, and Peterborough.

Manager Belinda Jones says the shop is now accepting donations of clothing, homeware, and toys between 9am and 4pm, Monday to Saturday. The team is also looking for new volunteers to help with the venture. Proceeds from the shop will fund essential services for those caring for family members or friends with long-term illnesses or disabilities. Further details are available on the charity’s website.

stories.headline: Shortage of preservative-free eye drops reported
stories.brief: Patients who rely on preservative-free eye drops may face supply issues. According to reports from The Pharmacist, three specific types of these products are currently out of stock. Residents across the Fens who use these medications are advised to check with their local pharmacy or GP if they are concerned about their current supply. No further details regarding the cause of the shortage or expected restock dates have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: New data released on NHS dental access for children in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: New figures have been published regarding NHS dental services for children across Ely and East Cambridgeshire. The data, reported by the Ely Standard, highlights the current state of access to dental care for young people in the region. Residents are encouraged to check the latest findings for details on how local provision is performing.

stories.headline: Police investigate reported assault at Cambridgeshire school
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Police are investigating an alleged assault involving a schoolboy. The incident is reported to have taken place at a school within the county. Authorities are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the event. No further details regarding the location of the school or the condition of the student have been released at this time.

stories.headline: New art exhibition opens at Wisbech Gallery
stories.brief:
A new exhibition featuring three local emerging artists has opened at the Wisbech Gallery. Titled Flare, the showcase displays work by Ruby Bellamy, Kayleigh Brooks, and Lily Rolfe, covering themes ranging from local landscapes to human emotions. The exhibition was opened by award-winning artist EVES and will remain on display until Saturday, November 28, 2026.

In addition to the exhibition, the gallery is hosting free weekly Sketch and Social sessions every Saturday throughout November from 11am to 3pm. The gallery is open to the public Wednesday through Saturday, between 10am and 4pm. Admission to both the exhibition and the social sessions is free of charge.

stories.headline: Progress continues on new Queen Elizabeth Hospital car park
stories.brief:
Construction of the new multi-storey car park at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn is reported to be progressing well. Project leaders confirm that the first stair core is now in place, reaching over 21 metres in height, with work on the steel foundations currently underway.

The £39 million facility is described as a vital enabling project for the future development of the hospital site. Once completed in late 2027, the six-storey building will provide space for 1,135 vehicles. The finished car park is set to include modern features such as smart signage, AI-enabled CCTV, LED motion-sensor lighting, and automatic number plate recognition technology.

stories.headline: Police investigate armed robbery at Long Sutton newsagent
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police are investigating an armed robbery at a newsagent in Long Sutton. A person armed with a knife entered the premises and stole a quantity of cash and cigarettes. Officers are currently looking into the incident. Anyone with information regarding the robbery is encouraged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Approval granted for 1,200 new homes in March
stories.brief: Plans have been approved for a major housing development in March. The project will see 1,200 new homes built, effectively extending the town. The decision follows reports from the BBC regarding the expansion. No further details on the construction timeline have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Thousands of crocus bulbs planted in King’s Lynn to support polio campaign
stories.brief:
Volunteers from the Rotary Club of Lynn have planted 16,000 purple crocus bulbs at the Edward Benefer Way roundabout. The display, completed on Sunday, November 8, aims to raise awareness for the global effort to eradicate polio. The purple flowers represent the dye used to mark children who have received immunisations. 

The project follows a similar planting event last year and recent efforts to highlight the Polio Plus campaign, including lighting up the Corn Exchange in purple. The bulbs were sponsored by Health and Community Construction, with additional support provided by the St James Health Centre. Rotary International has been working towards the global elimination of the disease since 1985.

stories.headline: March shopkeepers raise concerns over high street revamp
stories.brief: Business owners in March are reporting difficulties following recent changes to the town’s high street. According to reports from the BBC, local shopkeepers have linked their current trading struggles to the recent revamp project. No further details regarding the specific nature of the complaints or the response from local authorities have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn care home regains ‘good’ rating
stories.brief:
Amberley Hall Care Home in King’s Lynn has been rated ‘good’ by the Care Quality Commission following a recent inspection. The facility, located on Baldock Drive, has successfully exited special measures three years after previously being rated ‘inadequate’. 

Inspectors assessed the home across five key areas, including safety and leadership, finding that residents receive personalised care and are encouraged to maintain their independence. The report also highlighted improvements in care planning and the home’s partnership with the Integrated Care Board to support hospital discharges. Manager Blessy Masilamani credited the turnaround to the dedication and resilience of the staff team over the past year.

stories.headline: Public consultation launched for new Fenland PlayZones
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council is asking residents to share their views on proposals for two new multi-sports pitches. The council is working with the Football Foundation to develop PlayZones at West End Park in March and Wisbech Park. These floodlit, enclosed facilities are designed for sports including football, netball, and basketball.

Feedback from the public will be used to support funding applications and influence the design of the sites. Residents have until 11:59pm on Wednesday, November 25 to complete the online surveys. Paper copies are also available by emailing the council. Any future development remains subject to the standard planning permission process.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Metal Detecting Club raises funds for farming charity
stories.brief:
The King’s Lynn Metal Detecting Club has donated £665 to YANA, a charity that supports the farming community and those affected by depression. The funds were presented to volunteer Henry Kilvert during a club meeting on Tuesday. 

The total was raised through two sources: £130 collected from the sale of scrap lead gathered by members, and £535 from the sale of equipment belonging to the late Mike Turner. Mr. Turner, a long-standing member, had requested that proceeds from his equipment be donated to the charity. A club spokesperson said they were pleased to honour his wishes and thanked everyone who contributed to the final amount.

stories.headline: Peterborough murder trial hears evidence regarding knives
stories.brief: A man currently on trial for murder in Peterborough has told the court that he was carrying knives. The details were reported during proceedings at the city's crown court. No further information regarding the case or the identity of the defendant has been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire tech firms named in national awards
stories.brief: Several technology businesses based in Cambridgeshire and the wider East of England have been recognised in the latest Deloitte UK Technology Fast 50 list. The annual rankings highlight the fastest-growing companies within the sector across the country. Local firms were among those acknowledged for their recent performance in the industry.

stories.headline: Serial shoplifter jailed following Fenland store thefts
stories.brief: A serial shoplifter has been sentenced to time in prison after targeting a shop in the Fens on three consecutive days. The individual was convicted following the repeated thefts at the local business. No further details regarding the identity of the offender or the specific location of the shop have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Appeal launched for Golden Age Christmas gifts
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council and the group How Are You Fenland are asking for donations to support the Golden Age Christmas Appeal. Residents are invited to contribute gifts for older people in the community until Friday, December 4. Collection points are available at libraries in Wisbech, March, and Chatteris, as well as Tesco stores in Wisbech and March.

The collected items will be distributed at the Golden Age Fair on Friday, December 11. The event takes place at the Hudson Leisure Centre in Wisbech between 10am and 1pm, and entry is free. For further details, you can email goldenage@fenland.gov.uk or call 01354 654321.

stories.headline: MOT certificate from Princess Diana’s funeral hearse to be auctioned in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
An MOT certificate for the hearse that carried Princess Diana’s coffin to her final resting place is set to be sold at auction in King’s Lynn. The document relates to the Daimler DS420 vehicle used on September 6, 1997, to transport the Princess from Westminster Abbey to Althorp. 

The certificate will be offered at Anglia Car Auctions on Beveridge Way on Saturday, December 5. It is being sold in a frame alongside a photograph and two contemporary newspaper editions. The vendor has pledged that all proceeds from the sale will be donated to the Lennox Children’s Cancer Fund.

stories.headline: Cyclist seriously injured in Cambridgeshire hit and run
stories.brief: A cyclist has been left with serious injuries following a hit and run collision in a Cambridgeshire village. Police are investigating the incident, which involved a vehicle failing to stop at the scene. No further details regarding the exact location or the identity of those involved have been released at this time. Anyone with information is encouraged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: West Norfolk residents voice concerns over major infrastructure plans
stories.brief:
Residents in several West Norfolk villages are opposing large-scale developments, including the proposed Longmarsh solar farm and a new National Grid substation at Walpole. Concerns centre on the loss of agricultural land, potential environmental impacts, and increased heavy traffic near schools in West Walton. 

West Norfolk Council has scheduled an extraordinary meeting for November 16 at 5pm to discuss these issues. Meanwhile, a public consultation regarding the Walpole B substation project is open until December 8. Residents are encouraged to submit feedback on the National Grid website. With significant construction traffic expected on rural roads, local campaigners are calling for clarity on safety measures and the long-term impact of these infrastructure projects on their communities.

stories.headline: New warnings ordered for GLP-1 medication
stories.brief: Manufacturers of GLP-1 drugs have been instructed to include new safety warnings on their products. The updated labels will highlight the risk of a rare eye condition that has the potential to cause blindness. Patients currently using these medications are advised to be aware of this development. Further information regarding the specific drugs affected and the nature of the condition is expected to be provided by health authorities. Residents who have concerns about their current prescriptions should consult with their local GP or pharmacist for professional medical advice.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire film and television locations highlighted
stories.brief: A recent report from The Hunts Post has identified five locations across Cambridgeshire that have been used for film and television productions. The article highlights these sites as accessible destinations for members of the public to visit. Residents interested in local screen history can find further details regarding these specific filming spots in the original publication.

stories.headline: Police investigate potential links between ram raids
stories.brief: Police are investigating whether a series of ram raids in the region may be connected. Officers are currently looking into the incidents, which have been described as devastating. Authorities have not yet released further details regarding the specific locations or the timing of the offences. Residents are encouraged to remain vigilant and report any suspicious activity to the police.

stories.headline: Vehicle seized by police in Wisbech
stories.brief:
A driver in Wisbech has had their vehicle seized after being stopped by local police. Officers spotted the car travelling along Cromwell Road before the driver parked at the Tesco supermarket. Following checks, it was confirmed that the motorist did not have valid insurance for the vehicle.

Police are using the incident to remind the public of the consequences of driving uninsured. Penalties can include a three-hundred-pound fine and six points on a driving licence. In more serious cases, motorists could face an unlimited fine and a potential driving ban if the matter is taken to court.

stories.headline: Public consultation opens for King’s Lynn transport improvements
stories.brief:
Residents are being invited to share their views on a multi-million-pound project to upgrade travel routes in King’s Lynn. The scheme, which has secured nearly 21 million pounds in funding, aims to improve walking, cycling, and wheelchair access between the railway station, bus station, and town centre. Plans include infrastructure changes along Railway Road, Norfolk Street, and Blackfriars Street, alongside a redesign of Baxter’s Plain to include new seating and planting.

The public consultation remains open until midnight on Sunday, December 20. Residents can view the proposals and submit feedback online at the Norfolk County Council website, or attend drop-in sessions at Lynn Library on November 25 and December 3.

stories.headline: Ground Force star Tommy Walsh dies aged 69
stories.brief: The television personality Tommy Walsh has passed away at the age of 69. Known widely for his role on the popular gardening programme Ground Force, Mr Walsh maintained notable connections to Cambridgeshire throughout his life and career. Local reports have highlighted these special links to the county following the news of his death.

stories.headline: Police appeal following robbery in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Norfolk Police are appealing for witnesses after a man and a woman were assaulted during a robbery in King’s Lynn. The incident occurred on Portland Place at approximately 10pm last Saturday. A man attacked the pair with a metal bar before stealing their mobile phones and fleeing the scene. Both victims required hospital treatment for serious hand injuries.

Officers are asking anyone who witnessed the attack or possesses relevant CCTV, doorbell, or dashcam footage to come forward. You can contact Norfolk Police on 101 or report information online, quoting crime reference 451 of November 7. Anonymous reports can also be made through Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

stories.headline: Police investigate potential links between ram raids
stories.brief: Police are investigating a series of ram raids that have caused significant damage across the region. Officers are currently looking into the possibility that these incidents are connected. Authorities have described the impact of the raids as devastating for the local community. Anyone with information regarding these crimes is encouraged to contact the police.

stories.headline: Wisbech students win national award for hedgehog conservation business
stories.brief:
Three construction students from the College of West Anglia in Wisbech have achieved national success in the Peter Jones Foundation’s Tycoon Enterprise Competition. Finn McAuley, Marc Watson, and Erikas Rimkus, known as The Fabulous Baker’s Trio, secured joint first place in the Business for Good category. The students were recognised for their enterprise, which involves building hedgehog houses to provide safe shelter for local wildlife. 

The project, developed as part of their WorldSkills enterprise work, has also supported the local charity Ryston Rachel’s Hedgehog Hotel. College staff have praised the trio for their hard work, creativity, and commitment to environmental responsibility.

stories.headline: Pianist cycles through King’s Lynn to raise mental health awareness
stories.brief:
A musician travelling from Land’s End to John O’Groats has stopped in King’s Lynn as part of a nationwide cycling tour. James Tofalli is riding a quadricycle with a piano mounted on the back to raise awareness for mental health and autism. The 34-year-old, who turned to music to overcome drug addiction, has already covered over 761 miles on his journey. 

Mr Tofalli is using his not-for-profit company to provide pianos to communities and businesses across the UK. After his appearance on the High Street, he is now preparing to continue his trek towards Stamford and Newark, with plans to reach York by the end of November.

stories.headline: Highfield Littleport Academy faces potential transfer
stories.brief: Highfield Littleport Academy could be transferred to a new trust following a critical inspection by Ofsted. The school is currently facing the possibility of a change in management in the wake of the regulator's findings. No further details regarding the timeline for this potential transition or the specific concerns raised by inspectors have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police appeal for missing man Graeme
stories.brief: Police have issued an appeal for information regarding the whereabouts of a missing man named Graeme. Officers have stated they are increasingly concerned for his welfare. Anyone who may have seen him or who has information that could assist the authorities in locating him is urged to come forward.

stories.headline: Rail disruption between London and Peterborough
stories.brief: Rail services running between London and Peterborough are currently facing disruption. This follows an incident in which a person was struck by a train. Passengers are advised to check their travel plans before heading to the station, as delays are expected on the line. Further information regarding the status of services can be found on the National Rail website or through your local train operator.

stories.headline: Police appeal for information following East Cambridgeshire shoplifting
stories.brief: Officers in East Cambridgeshire are asking for the public's help to identify a man. Police wish to speak with him in connection with a reported shoplifting incident in the area. Anyone who may have information that could assist the investigation is encouraged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Police investigate potential links between ram raids
stories.brief: Police are investigating whether a series of ram raids could be connected. Officers are currently looking into the incidents, which have been described as devastating. No further details regarding the specific locations or the timing of these events have been released at this stage. Authorities are continuing their inquiries into the matter.

stories.headline: New dark comedy Wicker arrives at The Light in Wisbech
stories.brief: The dark, satirical comedy Wicker is now showing at The Light cinema in Wisbech. The film features performances from Olivia Colman, Peter Dinklage, and Alexander Skarsgård. Set in a medieval village, the story follows an ostracised fisherwoman who commissions a local basketmaker to create a husband for her. The resulting creation sparks jealousy and anger among the local villagers. The film, which also features Phil Daniels, explores themes of marriage and tradition through a mix of horror and sentimentality. Local cinema-goers can catch the film at The Light now.

stories.headline: Spire King’s Lynn Clinic marks one year of service
stories.brief:
The Spire King’s Lynn Clinic is celebrating its first anniversary after treating 1,200 patients. Located at Edward Benefer Way, the facility provides specialist healthcare to residents across West Norfolk. More than 30 consultants currently offer services ranging from orthopaedics and spinal surgery to cardiology and pain management. 

The clinic supports both private and NHS patients, aiming to provide expert care closer to home. While initial appointments are held locally, patients requiring surgery or further treatment are referred to Spire hospitals in Cambridge or Norwich. Clinic director Nayab Haider says the team is proud to have become a trusted part of the local healthcare community over the past twelve months.

stories.headline: New planning applications submitted across Fenland
stories.brief:
A range of new planning applications have been submitted to local councils across the Fens. Among the proposals is a project in Wisbech at 13 Alexandra Road, where plans have been lodged to convert and extend a building to create three houses and six flats. 

Other notable applications include the construction of three new homes on land south of 10 Sutton Road in Leverington, and a proposal for a new dwelling at Parsons Lane Drove. Additionally, the local fire station on Churchill Road in Wisbech has applied to install a back-up generator. Residents can view the full list of planning submissions through their local council’s planning portal.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn law firm raises over £2,000 for local charities
stories.brief:
A charity quiz hosted by law firm Fraser Dawbarns has raised a total of £2,520. The event, held at King’s Lynn Town Hall on October 22, saw teams compete to support two local causes: Breast of Friends and the West Norfolk Autism Group. Each charity received a donation of £1,260. 

The evening was hosted by the Mayor of West Norfolk, Councillor Steve Bearshaw. On the leaderboard, the team from Complete Commercial Finance secured the top spot. Both charities have been selected to receive ongoing support from the firm until April 2028. Organisers have already confirmed that the next annual quiz will take place on October 14, 2027.

stories.headline: Rail disruption between Peterborough and London
stories.brief: Rail services between Peterborough and London are currently facing disruption. This follows an incident in which a person was struck by a train. Passengers travelling across the region are advised to check for updates before they set off, as delays are expected on this busy route. Further information regarding the status of the line can be found through National Rail Enquiries or your local train operator.

stories.headline: Spalding church lighting display confirmed to return
stories.brief: A popular church lighting show in Spalding is set to go ahead as planned. Organisers have confirmed the event will proceed after successfully securing the necessary funding. The display, which has previously drawn significant interest from the local community, had faced uncertainty regarding its financial backing. Further details on the schedule for the upcoming show are expected to be released soon.

stories.headline: Ground Force star Tommy Walsh dies aged 69
stories.brief: The television presenter Tommy Walsh has died at the age of 69. Known for his role on the popular gardening programme Ground Force, Walsh had established connections to the Cambridgeshire area throughout his career. No further details regarding the circumstances of his death have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Wisbech residents gather for Remembrance Sunday parade
stories.brief:
Crowds gathered in Wisbech town centre on Sunday morning to mark Remembrance Day. The annual event, organised by the Town Council and the local branch of the Royal British Legion, saw cadets, armed forces members, and the public parade towards the war memorial at The Crescent.

Mayor Lucie Foice-Beard attended the service, which included the laying of wreaths and a two-minute silence at 11am. Among those paying their respects was 103-year-old veteran Stanley Eastgate. Local representatives praised the community for their support of the commemorations, which featured poppy displays throughout the town to honour those who lost their lives in service.

stories.headline: Inquest concludes into the death of North Lynn woman
stories.brief: An inquest at Norfolk Coroner’s Court has concluded that the death of 57-year-old Janina Daunaraviciute was alcohol-related. The North Lynn resident was found dead in her garden on Raby Avenue in the early hours of June 26. The court heard that Ms Daunaraviciute, an agency worker, had been struggling following the death of her husband last year. Her daughter told the hearing that her mother had appeared normal earlier that evening. A post-mortem examination confirmed the cause of death as hanging, with toxicology reports showing high levels of alcohol in her system. Area coroner Johanna Thompson offered her condolences to the family. If you are affected by these issues, you can contact Samaritans on 116 123.

stories.headline: Police provide update on Fenland park assault
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Police have issued an update regarding an alleged assault in a Fenland town park. The incident reportedly involved a victim being targeted with eggs. Authorities are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the event. No further details regarding the location or the identity of those involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Peterborough United Women’s FA Cup match abandoned
stories.brief:
A Peterborough United Women’s FA Cup fixture has been abandoned following a serious injury to a player. No further details regarding the incident or the player's condition have been released at this time. 

In separate club news, the Peterborough United Under-18s side secured a victory, highlighted by a hat-trick from one of their players.

stories.headline: Ely MP appointed to lead parliamentary group on flooding and drought
stories.brief: Ely MP Charlotte Cane has been elected to chair a parliamentary group focused on flooding and drought. The cross-party committee examines issues related to water management and environmental challenges across the country. Ms Cane will now head the group’s efforts in Westminster, where members work to address concerns regarding flood risks and water shortages.

stories.headline: Hundreds attend Remembrance Parade in March
stories.brief: Hundreds of people gathered in the Fenland town of March for the 2026 Remembrance Parade. The event saw members of the local community come together to pay their respects and honour the fallen.

stories.headline: Wisbech’s Luxe Cinema reopens following temporary closure
stories.brief:
The Luxe Cinema on Alexandra Road in Wisbech is welcoming customers back today. The venue had been closed since earlier this week due to what management described as unexpected circumstances. 

In a social media update this morning, a spokesperson confirmed that the cinema is now fully operational. The closure was necessary to allow for the renegotiation of the building's insurance policy, a process that has now been successfully completed. Doors are open for scheduled screenings from 1pm this afternoon.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn man fined after failed shoplifting attempt
stories.brief:
A 34-year-old father from Fairstead has been fined following a failed attempt to steal groceries from the Asda store in South Wootton. Brendon Smith, of William Booth Road, pleaded guilty at Lynn Magistrates’ Court to the theft of goods worth more than £400.

The court heard that on September 15, Smith and another man were intercepted by a security guard while attempting to drive away with the stolen items. The groceries were recovered at the scene. Smith was ordered to pay a total of £157, covering an £80 fine, a victim surcharge, and court costs. His co-offender did not appear in court.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire tourist spots recognised in national list
stories.brief: Several attractions across Cambridgeshire have been named among the best in the UK. According to a report by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the local sites were highlighted for their quality in a recent national ranking. While specific details regarding which locations were included have not been disclosed, the recognition places these Cambridgeshire destinations among the top-rated attractions in the country.

stories.headline: A look back at West Norfolk Bonfire Night celebrations
stories.brief:
Archive photographs have been released showcasing years of Bonfire Night celebrations across West Norfolk. The collection highlights various community events held since 2007, including the long-running Fawkes in the Walks display in King’s Lynn.

The images also feature firework events held in Hunstanton and near Downham Market, such as displays at Ryston and Stradsett Hall. The archive captures local festivities spanning nearly two decades, documenting the history of these annual gatherings for residents across the region.

stories.headline: Weather warning issued for Peterborough
stories.brief: A weather warning has been issued for the Peterborough area. Motorists are being advised to take extra care while travelling as the alert comes into force. Residents are encouraged to stay updated on the latest conditions and plan their journeys accordingly to ensure safety on the roads.

stories.headline: Yellow weather warning issued for dense fog in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A yellow weather warning for dense fog has been issued for Cambridgeshire. Residents across the Fens are advised to take care while travelling, as visibility may be significantly reduced. Motorists should allow extra time for their journeys and ensure their lights are working correctly. Please stay tuned to Fenland Angels Radio for any further updates regarding local travel conditions throughout the day.

stories.headline: Fire crews tackle blaze at former hotel in March
stories.brief: Emergency services are currently dealing with a significant fire at a former hotel in March. Officials have warned that the building is at risk of collapse due to the severity of the blaze. Residents in the area are advised to take care while the incident is ongoing. There are no further details available at this time regarding the cause of the fire or any potential injuries. We will bring you more updates on this developing story as information becomes available.

stories.headline: North Lynn mechanic banned after A17 traffic stop
stories.brief: A North Lynn mechanic has been disqualified from driving for six months following an incident on the A17. Police stopped 39-year-old Jevgenijus Levinskas on April 20 after noticing he was driving a vehicle insured to someone else. Officers discovered Levinskas was using false number plates to conceal the fact that he did not hold a valid driving licence. A search of the car also uncovered a quantity of the Class B drug Cathinone. At Lynn Magistrates’ Court, Levinskas pleaded guilty to multiple driving offences and drug possession. He was issued a £120 fine and received six penalty points, resulting in a driving ban after exceeding the 12-point limit.

stories.headline: Debate continues over Cambridgeshire council reorganisation
stories.brief: Cambridge City Council has identified "Option B" as the preferred approach for reorganising the seven local authorities across Cambridgeshire. The proposal is currently being put forward as the most effective way to restructure the county's existing council system. No further details regarding the specific changes or the timeline for implementation have been provided at this stage. Residents are advised to monitor official council communications for updates on how these potential administrative shifts might impact local services across the region.

stories.headline: Liberal Democrats gain control of county council
stories.brief: The Liberal Democrats have secured control of the county council. The change in leadership follows the latest election results.

stories.headline: North Lynn pair deny animal neglect charges
stories.brief:
Two people from North Lynn have appeared at Lynn Magistrates’ Court to deny charges of causing prolonged neglect to a dog. Mark Ogle, aged 35, and 41-year-old Jade Kennett, both of Walpole Road, entered not guilty pleas regarding an incident alleged to have occurred on June 25. 

Ms Kennett also denied a separate charge of using threatening words to cause alarm or distress on June 24. The case has been adjourned until January 7 to allow for further communication between the Crown Prosecution Service and the RSPCA. Mr Ogle has been released on unconditional bail, while Ms Kennett remains on bail with conditions preventing her from contacting the alleged victim of the threatening behaviour.

stories.headline: Peterborough United knocked out of FA Cup
stories.brief: Peterborough United have been eliminated from the FA Cup following a heavy defeat. The team lost 5-0 to Reading in their latest fixture.

stories.headline: Search underway for missing 69-year-old man from March
stories.brief:
Police have expressed concern for the welfare of a 69-year-old man who has been reported missing from March. Authorities are currently looking for the individual and are urging anyone with information regarding his whereabouts to come forward. 

Residents across the Fens are asked to remain vigilant and report any potential sightings to the police immediately. Further updates will be provided as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Waterstones names festive mystery as Book of the Week
stories.brief: A festive murder mystery novella has been selected as the Book of the Week at the Waterstones branch in King’s Lynn. Titled The Case of the Christmas Card by author Elly Griffiths, the story follows time-travelling detective Ali Dawson. In the book, Dawson finds herself hosting Charles Dickens while investigating the death of an artist and the disappearance of a friend's daughter. The pair must work together to solve these mysteries before Christmas Day. The title is currently featured as a top pick for the start of November at the local bookshop.

stories.headline: Peterborough knocked out of FA Cup
stories.brief: Peterborough United have been eliminated from the FA Cup following a heavy defeat against Reading. The match saw Charlie Savage play against a side managed by his father, Robbie Savage, as Reading secured a decisive victory over the Peterborough team.

stories.headline: Knife monument to visit Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A sculpture created from knives is set to visit Cambridgeshire. According to the county’s constabulary, the monument is described as a powerful installation. Further details regarding the exact location and dates for the arrival of the artwork have not yet been released. Residents are advised to keep an eye on official police channels for updates on when and where the monument will be displayed.

stories.headline: Coronation Fountain to be unveiled in March
stories.brief: A new Coronation Fountain is set to be unveiled in the town of March. The project, located in the Cambridgeshire town, is now complete and ready for its official reveal. Further details regarding the unveiling ceremony have not yet been announced.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn runner to complete 45 festive fancy dress runs
stories.brief:
A King’s Lynn athlete is preparing for a demanding fundraising challenge throughout December. Matty Parker, a member of Ryston Runners, plans to complete 45 separate 5km runs while wearing a different fancy dress costume for each outing. The initiative, titled December Dashes, aims to raise funds and awareness for the charity Caring Together, which supports unpaid carers.

Mr. Parker intends to visit various locations across the region, including St Ives and Swaffham, and hopes to be joined by fellow runners. His challenge concludes on New Year’s Eve at RAF Marham. Supporters can contribute to his fundraising appeal via the JustGiving website.

stories.headline: Peterborough United defeated by Reading
stories.brief: Peterborough United suffered a heavy defeat at home yesterday, losing five-nil to Reading. The result was confirmed following the latest fixture between the two sides. Fans looking for a detailed breakdown of individual performances can find player ratings published by The Tilehurst End.

stories.headline: Police appeal following incident on Cambridgeshire train
stories.brief:
British Transport Police are investigating reports of an indecent exposure on a train travelling through Cambridgeshire. Officers were alerted after a man allegedly exposed himself while seated at a table on board the service. 

Authorities are now looking into the circumstances surrounding the incident. Anyone with relevant information regarding the event is encouraged to contact the British Transport Police to assist with their ongoing enquiries.

stories.headline: Plans submitted for 125 new homes in March
stories.brief: Proposals have been put forward for a new housing development in March. The plans involve the construction of 125 homes on a field within the town. Further details regarding the project are expected as the planning process continues.

stories.headline: Three-year driving ban for King’s Lynn drug-driver
stories.brief:
A 35-year-old man from King’s Lynn has been disqualified from driving for three years after testing positive for cannabis. Harry Burt, of Persimmon in Fairstead, was stopped by police on Queensway in Gaywood while driving without insurance. A roadside test revealed he had double the legal limit of THC in his system.

At Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Burt pleaded guilty to drug-driving, driving without insurance, and possession of cannabis. The court heard he had consumed the drug to assist with sleep. In addition to the driving ban, Burt was ordered to pay a total of £634 in fines, costs, and a victim surcharge.

stories.headline: Peterborough United face Reading in FA Cup clash
stories.brief: Peterborough United are set to play Reading in the FA Cup. Fans looking to follow the match can find details regarding kick-off times, live streaming options, and television coverage through the Radio Times. The publication has provided a guide for supporters wanting to watch the fixture.

stories.headline: Police investigate ram raid in Littleport
stories.brief: Police are searching for suspects following a ram raid involving an ATM in Littleport. Officers were called to the scene after the incident occurred. An investigation into the theft is currently underway. Anyone with information regarding the raid is encouraged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Cash machine stolen in petrol station ram-raid
stories.brief: Police are investigating after a cash machine was stolen from a petrol station. The incident involved a ram-raid, where the suspects used a vehicle to gain access to the premises. Authorities have not yet released details regarding the location of the petrol station or the identity of those involved. Investigations into the theft are currently ongoing. Anyone with information regarding the incident is encouraged to contact the police.

stories.headline: Significant improvements noted at Gaywood’s Parkway Academy
stories.brief:
Parkway Academy in Gaywood has been recognised for significant progress following a recent Ofsted inspection. Formerly known as Howard Junior School, the academy joined the Eastern Multi-Academy Trust in December 2023 following a period of instability. Inspectors visiting on October 6 and 7 praised the school’s leadership and governance, noting that expected standards are now being met across areas including teaching, attendance, and pupil behaviour. 

The report highlights that confidence and belief within the school community have been successfully rebuilt. Principal Ben Paull and the trust were commended for their rapid actions in creating a positive, supportive culture. The academy, which underwent a name change and uniform update this September, is now described as a place where pupils are thriving.

stories.headline: Peterborough and Reading football match scheduled for November 7th
stories.brief: Football fans are looking ahead to a fixture between Peterborough and Reading. The match is scheduled to take place on the 7th of November, 2026. Details regarding the game have been noted by sports reporting services.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over East Cambridgeshire data centre expansion
stories.brief: Plans to increase the size of a data centre in East Cambridgeshire have prompted concerns. The proposal to scale up the facility is currently under discussion, though specific details regarding the project’s scope or location have not been disclosed. Residents and local stakeholders are now considering the potential impact of the development. We will bring you further updates on this story as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Daytime delays expected on A47 at King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Drivers using the A47 in King’s Lynn are being warned of potential disruption starting this Monday, November 9. National Highways is carrying out bridge survey work on the Great Ouse Bridge, which will require daytime lane closures between the Pullover and Hardwick roundabouts. The work is scheduled to continue until December 4.

While no official diversions are in place, motorists should allow extra time for their journeys. Officials note that the project is weather-dependent and could change at short notice. Previously planned night closures for this stretch have been cancelled for now. For the latest travel updates, residents are advised to check the National Highways website.

stories.headline: South Cambridgeshire residents raise concerns over East West Rail project
stories.brief: Residents in South Cambridgeshire have expressed significant concerns regarding the potential impact of the East West Rail project. Local people are calling for greater transparency and have formally demanded to see the business case for the proposed development. Those living in the area have described the potential consequences of the scheme as devastating. There has been no further comment from the project organisers at this stage.

stories.headline: Chatteris identified as location for new reservoir
stories.brief: A report from the March Chatteris Whittlesey News has highlighted the town of Chatteris as being situated on the edge of a new reservoir project. The development is being described as England’s newest reservoir. No further details regarding the construction timeline or the specific impact on the local area have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Police appeal following King’s Lynn hit-and-run
stories.brief:
Norfolk Police are appealing for witnesses after a collision in King’s Lynn on Wednesday evening. At approximately 5pm, a black Porsche was observed weaving through traffic on London Road before striking a grey MG. The driver of the Porsche failed to stop at the scene and left the area. 

Fortunately, no injuries were reported following the incident. Officers are now working to trace the driver involved. Anyone who witnessed the collision or has relevant information is asked to contact Norfolk Police quoting reference 1837166. Details can also be provided anonymously through Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

stories.headline: Government labels Peterborough street fireworks unacceptable
stories.brief: The government has described the recent use of fireworks on streets in Peterborough as unacceptable. The statement follows reports regarding the public use of pyrotechnics in the city. No further details regarding specific incidents or potential enforcement actions have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Financial support scheme available for families in the Fens
stories.brief: A new initiative is offering financial assistance to eligible families to help with the cost of healthy food and milk. The scheme aims to support households in purchasing essential nutritional items. Residents are encouraged to check their eligibility for the programme to see if they qualify for this additional help. Further details regarding the application process and specific criteria for the support are available through the Fenland Citizen.

stories.headline: Police drones deployed at Long Sutton building site
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police have deployed drones to a construction site in Long Sutton. Officers were called to the location to assist with operations at the development. No further details regarding the nature of the incident or any potential outcomes have been released by authorities at this time.

stories.headline: Community raises £90,000 for Fenland church spire
stories.brief: A fundraising campaign has reached its target of £90,000 to help preserve a historic church spire in the Fens. Local residents contributed the funds to support the repair project, which aims to secure the future of the landmark structure. The effort has been described as a significant community achievement.

stories.headline: Gaywood man sentenced for threatening King’s Lynn job centre staff
stories.brief:
A 48-year-old man from Gaywood has appeared in court after making threats towards security staff at the King’s Lynn job centre. James Evans, of South Lynn Road, pleaded guilty to causing distress following an incident on September 21. The court heard that Evans became aggressive during a visit regarding his disability payments, telling a security officer he would find out where they lived and post it online. 

Representing the defendant, solicitor Andrew Cogan stated that Evans had been distressed by a reduction in his benefits. Magistrates at the town’s court ordered Evans to pay £50 in compensation to the victim.
